rulings.challenge_claim: One item: the row's observed_substrate_signals names a koh-amar speech formula that occurs nowhere within Jer.13.20-13.27, the seam and the typing being otherwise byte-sound. The converging item raises the same formula defect and three more: the opening seam's person-shift warrant is not delivered at the opening of 13:20, the woe-lexeme contrast carries a byte-false form label at 22:13 and 23:1, and two byte-true catchwords straddle the row's own opening seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The formula arm is the SAME defect in both items; the other three are distinct and additional. Formula (upheld): the census object koh amar YHWH returns 152 verses (sweep: 152 verses; with the single adonai-YHWH stack at 7:20 the census is 153), and its chapter-13 sites are 13:1, 13:9, 13:12 and 13:13 (sweep: 4 verses in the chapter), all standing before the span, the next site at 14:10 — none falls inside 13:20-13:27, so the declared signal has no support in the span's own bytes. The span's actual divine formula is נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.25, byte tier). Person shift (upheld): 13:20 opens שאי שְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ וראי וּרְא֔וּ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier for the pointed members; the two ketiv members stand unpointed in the source), a doubled-note verse in the single-witness inventory whose two notes sit on the two opening imperatives — feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere — with the intervening object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) carrying a masculine-plural suffix under either reading. The feminine-singular forms לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) stand in the verse's second half, so the shift is not what 13:20 opens with. The run the row actually splices, הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), is a definite masculine-plural participle with a prepositional phrase and carries no addressee marking at all, while the English paired with it, “Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north” (web:Jer.13.20), renders the contested imperatives that lie OUTSIDE the splice: gloss extent exceeds splice extent at exactly the point the warrant turns on. Recording the note as consulted but not spliced is a mark disclosure, not an answer to the reading it complicates. Form label (upheld): 22:13 and 23:1 each open on bare ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.13 and oshb:Jer.23.1, byte tier) as the verse's first token; the vav-prefixed shape וְה֥וֹי (oshb:Jer.34.5, byte tier) stands at two verses (sweep: 2 verses — 22:18 and 34:5), both funeral cries, so calling the 22:13 and 23:1 onsets vav-prefixed is contradicted by their own bytes. The oy digit is right: that lexeme is token-bound at 8 verses (sweep: 8 verses — 4:13, 6:4, 10:19, 13:27, 18:17, 30:14, 31:16, 48:46), against 14 for a bare consonantal substring (sweep: 14 verses). Cohesion (upheld): תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier) closes 13:18 and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) closes 13:20, that stem standing at 4 verses (sweep: 4 verses — 13:11, 13:18, 13:20, 33:9); עֵ֥דֶר (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier) closes 13:17 and הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) stands inside 13:20, that noun at 6 verses (sweep: 6 verses — 6:3, 13:17, 13:20, 31:10, 31:24, 51:23). Both straddle the row's own opening seam, and conceding shared imagery in the rejected alternative is not disclosure of a byte-true device. The seam itself survives — the feminine-singular Jerusalem address does govern 13:20b through the explicit vocative at 13:27 — but the stated ground, the sole cited splice, one of the two declared signals and a named form class are all byte-defective. Parashah disclosure is accurate as written (setumah at 13:19 ahead of the opening, petuchah at 13:27 at the close; single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and the span carries no paseq seg.
rulings.remedy: No respan; the cut at 13:20 stands. (1) boundary_rationale: restate the opening ground where the bytes put it — 13:20 opens with the doubled-note imperative pair (feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere) and a masculine-plural object, and the feminine-singular address begins mid-verse at the 'to you' and 'your glory' forms and then governs through the vocative at 13:27; say that the note falls on the very forms the person reading turns on, rather than logging it as consulted-but-not-spliced. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the splice so the spliced extent covers exactly what the paired English renders, then re-collate at byte tier. (3) boundary_rationale: strike 'vav-prefixed' from the woe contrast — 22:13 and 23:1 open on bare hoy as their first token, and the vav-prefixed shape stands at 22:18 and 34:5 (sweep: 2 verses), both funeral cries. (4) observed_substrate_signals: remove speech_formula.koh_amar (no koh-amar verse falls in 13:20-13:27; the chapter's four sites are 13:1, 13:9, 13:12, 13:13); if a divine-formula signal is wanted the span's token is the neum-YHWH at 13:25. (5) device_notes or strongest_rejected_alternative: disclose and answer the two straddling catchwords with their swept objects and digits (the glory stem, sweep: 4 verses; the flock noun, sweep: 6 verses). (6) The signal field is dependent on the driver, so striking one entry re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence. TEST the cure must pass: no koh-amar verse inside the span on the named census object; every form-class label re-read off the pointed bytes at its own site; each straddling device named with object and digit; splice extent equal to gloss extent on every pairing.

rulings.challenge_claim: The topical-header claim is byte-sound, but a ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed while the row makes a positive absence statement for the parashah layer; secondarily, the appeal to how header-bounded units elsewhere carry their attached content as one piece is uneven across the four attested sites.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the bytes, with one finding added. Disclosure: 14:3, inside the span, carries one note in the single-witness inventory and it stands in the verse as unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, צעוריהם צְעִירֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.14.3, byte tier for the pointed member). The row's device_notes state positively that no verse within 14:1-14:6 carries a parashah mark — true on the inventory, as is the petuchah at 13:27 ahead of the row — so one single-witness layer is engaged with a positive absence claim while a present item in the other, the largest such inventory in this book (141 notes over 124 verses), goes unmentioned; that asymmetry is what the span-relevant disclosure rule exists to catch. The header object and digit are sound and are NOT disturbed: the shape carrying the prophet's name returns 14:1, 46:1, 47:1 and 49:34 (sweep: 4 verses), and dropping the name widens the result to five by admitting the to-him variant in the superscription at 1:2 (sweep: 5 verses), so the needle is correctly bounded and not blended with the eleven-verse prose-sermon shape. Secondary arm upheld: 46:1 reads “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) and heads the whole nations collection rather than bundling an attached description, while 47:1 and 49:34 head single-nation oracles each with its own attached setting — the cross-site analogy needs a per-site read. NEW FINDING, raised by neither item: gloss extent and splice extent come apart in the same sentence. The splice ends at דִּבְרֵ֖י (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) while the English paired with it, “This is Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought” (web:Jer.14.1), renders הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) as well — one token past the spliced extent. The span carries no paseq seg, so nothing is owed there.
rulings.remedy: No respan; the header seam and the 4-verse digit stand. (1) device_notes: add the ketiv/qere note at 14:3 (single-witness), stated as its own layer and kept distinct from the parashah sentence, which is accurate and stays as written. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the header splice so it ends where the paired English ends — extend the splice through the drought noun or trim the English to stop before it — then re-collate at byte tier. (3) boundary_rationale: replace the blanket cross-site analogy with a per-site statement (46:1 heads the nations collection rather than bundling a description; 47:1 and 49:34 head single-nation oracles with their own attached settings), or drop the analogy and rest the bundling on the span's own absence of an addressee or scene shift through 14:6. TEST the cure must pass: span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry clean across BOTH single-witness layers for every verse of 14:1-14:6; the re-cut splice re-collates at byte tier with gloss extent equal to splice extent; every cross-site claim names its own site.

rulings.challenge_claim: The one-verse boundary is defensible, but the frame-owner ground given for it is contradicted by the run the row itself splices, and the verse's third-person handling of the divine name means describing it as the deity answering the plea over-specifies the mouth.
rulings.grounds: The first arm is upheld on the bytes; the second is real as an observation but wrongly framed as a defect. Upheld: the row's stated ground is that the pronouncement is spoken about the people rather than to them, but the continuation inside its own splice, לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), is a lamed phrase marking the people as the party addressed, and the row's own paired English reads “Yahweh says to this people” (web:Jer.14.10). The third-person forms the row leans on — אָֽהֲבוּ֙, רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם, עֲוֺנָ֔ם, חַטֹּאתָֽם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier) — mark the oracle's SUBJECT, not its addressee, so the single sentence carrying the boundary conflates subject person with addressee. Corrected: the second arm's byte facts hold — 14:10 carries no first-person clause (its finite verbs are third person) and refers to the divine name in the third person inside the quotation, וַיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א רָצָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), while the first first-person divine clauses in this stretch stand at 14:12, אֵינֶ֤נִּי שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ and אָנֹכִ֖י מְכַלֶּ֥ה (oshb:Jer.14.12, byte tier) — but they do not make the mouth over-specified. The verse opens on the messenger formula naming the speaker, which is exactly what frame-ownership discipline requires, and third-person self-reference inside a messenger-formula oracle is an ordinary shape, not a misattributed mouth. The defect is therefore one sentence's category conflation, not a frame-owner error. The boundary is not disturbed, and the span's disclosure is in fact complete: setumah at 14:9 ahead of the row and setumah at 14:10 itself (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), with no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg on 14:10.
rulings.remedy: No respan; the one-verse unit stands. (1) boundary_rationale: rewrite the footing sentence so addressee and subject are not conflated — 14:10 is addressed TO the people (the lamed phrase inside the row's own splice, matched by the paired English) and speaks ABOUT them in the third person; the seam's real footing change is that 14:7-9 addresses the deity, 14:10 addresses the people, and 14:11 turns to private address to the prophet. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: apply the same correction to 'the addressee shifts from Yahweh-as-hearer to the people-as-subject', which mixes the two categories in one clause; state addressee-to-addressee. (3) device_notes, optional: note that the oracle body refers to the divine name in the third person and carries no first-person clause, the first such clause standing at 14:12. TEST the cure must pass: no sentence in any field assigns one clause both roles, and every addressee claim is carried by a form inside the cited splice, with no token in that same splice contradicting it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The formula the row cuts on recurs verse-initially at 14:14 inside its own span, undisclosed, and the reason given for keeping that turn internal is contradicted by the bytes of 14:13-14:14; on those bytes either 14:14 is a seam or the criterion applied at 15:1 does not hold.
rulings.grounds: Two arms upheld, the third corrected, and one further defect the item itself misses. Upheld: the opening shape וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.14.11, byte tier) stands verse-initially again at 14:14, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.14.14, byte tier), inside the row's own span, and again at 15:1, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.1, byte tier), the three differing only in accents; the shape returns 13 verses (sweep: 13 verses — 1:7, 1:9, 1:12, 1:14, 3:6, 3:11, 11:6, 11:9, 13:6, 14:11, 14:14, 15:1, 24:3). The row names 14:14 only as a doubled-note site and never as a recurrence of the device carrying its own boundary. Upheld: the rejected alternative's blanket sentence, that neither internal turn carries an addressee or scene change of its own, is byte-false for 14:14 — 14:13 is the prophet addressing the deity, וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.13, byte tier), and 14:14 is the deity answering him, so the addressee does alternate across that turn. Corrected: the dichotomy does not follow. The seam at 14:22 into 15:1 is not carried by the formula shape alone — the material closing at 14:22 is a first-common-plural communal plea addressed to the deity, a different speaker role and a different unit type from a private prophet-and-deity dialogue, and it closes on a petuchah (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, corroboration only) — whereas across 14:13 into 14:14 the same two participants continue one sustained private exchange, which under the ruled granularity is a speaker turn and not a tier-1 internal seam. The criterion therefore survives; what fails is the row's blanket sentence and its silence about the recurrence. NEW FINDING: the item's own statement that disclosure is otherwise complete here is byte-false. Two paseq segs fall inside the span, at 14:13 and at 14:16 (single-witness, count-only — no intra-verse position is sourceable from that layer), and neither is disclosed. What the row does carry is accurate: setumah at 14:12, 14:13 and 14:14 within the span, setumah at 14:10 ahead of it, and the doubled note at 14:14.
rulings.remedy: No respan; 14:14 need not become a seam. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'neither carries an addressee or scene change of its own' with the byte-true statement — 14:13 is the prophet addressing the deity and 14:14 the deity answering him, so the addressee does alternate — and give the ground that actually holds the exchange together: both turns stay inside one sustained private exchange between the same two participants, whereas the seam four verses on additionally carries a speaker-role change from a communal first-common-plural plea, a different unit type, and a petuchah at 14:22 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only). (2) boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose that the opening formula shape recurs verse-initially at 14:14 inside the span (sweep: 13 verses book-wide) and say why the recurrence is not cut, since the same shape carries the onset at 15:1. (3) device_notes: add the two paseq segs at 14:13 and 14:16 (single-witness, count-only; assert no intra-verse position) beside the parashah and ketiv/qere disclosures already carried. (4) confidence and frontier_flag_considered: re-open both once the rejected-alternative ground is restated, since the discarded rival is stronger than the present sentence concedes. TEST the cure must pass: no sentence denies a feature the span's own bytes carry; every span-relevant single-witness layer is disclosed for every verse of the span; a device that carries the row's own boundary and recurs inside the span is named with its digit and answered.

rulings.challenge_claim: The seam driver is a form-class misidentification — the opening word of 14:17 is a waw-consecutive perfect, not an imperative — and the same construction runs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the pointed bytes, and it bites harder than the item frames it. Form class: 14:17 opens וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier) — vav with sheva, alef with qamats, mem with patah, resh with sheva, and a final tav carrying dagesh and qamats, the second-masculine-singular suffix-conjugation ending. The form is waw plus perfect, not a morphological imperative. The second-masculine-singular imperative of this verb stands three verses earlier at 13:18, אֱמֹ֥ר (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), with no such ending, and the discourse-frame imperative class that may drive a seam is instanced by true plural imperatives at 4:5 and 10:1. No morphology layer is staged, so this is argued from the pointing plus both witnesses' renderings, which read a modal continuation rather than a command. The weight: the row asserts the class in boundary_rationale AND carries speech_formula.discourse_imperative as its single declared substrate signal, so the mislabel leaves the row with no sound declared driver, and that field is dependent on the driver. Not seam-exclusive: the construction וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier) returns 18 verses (sweep: 18 verses — 5:19, 7:28, 8:4, 11:3, 13:12, 13:13, 14:17, 15:2, 16:11, 17:20, 19:11, 23:33, 25:27, 25:28, 25:30, 26:4, 38:26, 43:10) and the bare form 30 verses (sweep: 30 verses); at 15:2 it sits mid-verse inside a conditional as an ordinary continuation, וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), four verses on in the same stretch. What does NOT follow is a respan: reading 14:17 as mere continuation of the divine speech begun at 14:14 is a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, and the cut is re-groundable without one — 14:14-16 is divine speech to the prophet ABOUT the prophets and the people, while 14:17 commissions a word for delivery TO them, and both witnesses open a fresh quoted message there. The item is also right that 14:16, just ahead of the opening, carries no parashah mark, so no tier-3 corroboration is available at this seam. NEW FINDING: the same construction stands verse-initially at 13:12 and again at 13:13, adjacent verses in the same stretch and both inside the 18-verse set, so the mislabel class reaches past this row.
rulings.remedy: No respan. (1) observed_substrate_signals: replace speech_formula.discourse_imperative — the form is a waw-prefixed second-masculine-singular suffix conjugation, not an imperative — with a dotted key matching what the bytes carry (a speech-delivery command opening a fresh quoted message, or the change in who the message is addressed to across 14:16 into 14:17). (2) boundary_rationale: strike 'A fresh discourse-frame imperative opens the row'; state the form as the pointed bytes carry it and re-ground the seam on the delivery command plus the addressee change, and disclose that the same construction recurs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force and is attested at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), so it is not seam-exclusive. (3) Dependent fields: this is the row's single declared signal, so its replacement re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence. (4) device_notes: state plainly that 14:16 carries no parashah mark, so this seam has no tier-3 corroboration, rather than leaving it implied. (5) CORPUS-WIDE ORDER, carried as its own sweep and not folded into this row's fix: sweep all 18 sites of the delivery construction (5:19, 7:28, 8:4, 11:3, 13:12, 13:13, 14:17, 15:2, 16:11, 17:20, 19:11, 23:33, 25:27, 25:28, 25:30, 26:4, 38:26, 43:10) plus the 30-verse bare set, and correct every row that labels this waw-perfect an imperative or a discourse-frame imperative, or that rests a seam on its supposed exclusivity — the verse-initial occurrences at 13:12 and 13:13 are the nearest instances. TEST the cure must pass: every form-class label re-read off the pointed bytes at its own site, with the imperative at 13:18 as the contrasting control; no seam-exclusivity claim for a construction whose sweep digit and site list are not stated beside it.

rulings.challenge_claim: A ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed in the very clause the row cites, and the span description merges two fourfold lists that the bytes keep apart.
rulings.grounds: Both arms upheld on the bytes, with one framing detail corrected. Disclosure: 15:4, inside the span, carries one note in the single-witness inventory standing in the verse as unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, לזועה לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.4, byte tier for the pointed member), and it is nowhere disclosed, while the row's device_notes state positively that nothing within 15:1-15:4 carries a parashah mark — true on the inventory, as is the petuchah at 14:22 ahead of the row. Detail corrected: the note does not sit in the clause the row names. The closing sentence cites 15:4 by its Manasseh clause, and the variant stands in the verse's first clause; what carries the obligation is that the verse lies inside the span and is cited at all, not which clause was named. Count objects: the fourfold assignment lies wholly inside 15:2 — אֲשֶׁ֨ר לַמָּ֤וֶת לַמָּ֨וֶת֙ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לַחֶ֨רֶב֙ לַחֶ֔רֶב וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לָֽרָעָב֙ לָֽרָעָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לַשְּׁבִ֖י לַשֶּֽׁבִי (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier) — four pairs in one verse. 15:3 carries a DIFFERENT and separately numbered quartet, אַרְבַּ֤ע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ (oshb:Jer.15.3, byte tier), whose members are sword, dogs, birds and beasts, and the numeral stands there and not in 15:2; so attributing one fourfold assignment of death, sword, famine and captivity to 15:2-15:3 blends two count objects and attaches the numeral's home verse to the wrong list. The row's uncontested calls check out: 15:3 carries the postpositive נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.3, byte tier), and the koh-amar inside 15:2 — itself a census site — is embedded in speech the prophet is told to relay rather than a fresh divine onset, so declining to cut there is right. The span carries no paseq seg. The delivery construction recurring mid-verse at 15:2, which the item leaves unremarked, is the same defect class ruled at 14:17 and is carried there as a corpus-wide sweep rather than duplicated here.
rulings.remedy: No respan; the 15:1 onset and the uncut koh-amar at 15:2 stand. (1) device_notes: add the ketiv/qere note at 15:4 (single-witness), stated as its own layer and kept distinct from the parashah sentence, which is accurate and stays. (2) boundary_rationale: split the conflated citation — the fourfold death, sword, famine and captivity assignment lies wholly in 15:2, while 15:3 carries a separately numbered quartet of four kinds (sword, dogs, birds, beasts) and is where the numeral stands; name each list with its own verse and its own count object, and carry no digit across both. TEST the cure must pass: span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry clean across parashah AND ketiv/qere for every verse of 15:1-15:4; every enumerated list in prose names its own verse and its own swept object, with no numeral attached to a list it does not stand in.
